title: Deep-Layer Attention Pruning for Vision-Language Models

contributions.purpose: Prune visual tokens for efficient VLM inference on spatially-sensitive tasks without offline calibration.
contributions.mechanism: Extract text-to-vision attention from a deeper LLM layer (layer 12 of 32 in InternVL2.5-8B) instead of shallow layers, and apply Maximal Independent Set (MIS) selection directly with no debiasing.
contributions.evaluation: Achieves 66.32% average grounding accuracy on RefCOCO/RefCOCO+/RefCOCOg (10% token retention), surpassing D2Pruner (55.03%) by +11.29 points while retaining 92% of no-pruning performance.
contributions.domain: Vision-language model inference efficiency / visual token pruning for grounding
contributions.source_quote: We demonstrate that deep-layer attention pruning achieves 66.32% grounding accuracy on RefCOCO benchmarks, surpassing the state-of-the-art D2Pruner by +11.29 points while retaining 92% of no-pruning performance.

contributions.purpose: Remove the offline calibration requirement of prior debiasing methods.
contributions.mechanism: Operate fully online using only the current input's deep-layer attention, avoiding the offline bias prior D2Pruner computes from 1000 COCO images.
contributions.evaluation: Matches/exceeds D2Pruner accuracy (66.32% vs 55.03%) with no external calibration data.
contributions.domain: Vision-language model inference efficiency / visual token pruning for grounding
contributions.source_quote: We eliminate the need for offline calibration data, enabling simpler deployment without domain-specific priors.

contributions.purpose: Explain why prior ratio-based debiasing is unnecessary (and harmful).
contributions.mechanism: Phase-0 diagnostic analysis measuring the Spearman correlation between attention and token position across layers, plus an ablation applying the ratio formula A_mid/(A_shallow+eps) at multiple layers.
contributions.evaluation: Position correlation is uniformly weak (Spearman rho ~0.17, range 0.143-0.179, below the 0.3 threshold); ratio debiasing degrades accuracy everywhere (-25.46pp at L4, -11.69pp at L12), refuting the shallow-layer-as-debiasing-prior hypothesis.
contributions.domain: Vision-language model inference efficiency / visual token pruning for grounding
contributions.source_quote: We provide diagnostic analysis showing that shallow-layer attention lacks the positional bias assumed by prior debiasing approaches, explaining why ratio-based normalization degrades rather than improves performance.

self_declared_provenance.quote: While prior methods like D2Pruner extract attention from shallow layers (L2) and apply offline debiasing, we show that attention at layer 12 of InternVL2.5-8B is semantically rich enough to directly guide token selection without any debiasing.

Beyond simple top-k selection, D2Pruner (Zhang et al., 2025) introduces Maximal Independent Set (MIS) selection to ensure spatial diversity among retained tokens ... Our approach is straightforward: extract attention weights from layer 12 ... and apply MIS selection directly without any debiasing.

recent analysis (Yin et al., 2025) reveals that visual information flow in MLLMs varies significantly across layers, suggesting that layer choice is critical for attention-based pruning. Our work builds on these insights by demonstrating that deep-layer attention eliminates the need for explicit debiasing.

notes: Reports its own failed hypothesis (shallow-layer attention as an online debiasing prior collapses to 13.24% vs 38.70%) as motivation; the positive result is essentially D2Pruner's MIS selection applied at layer 12 instead of layer 2, i.e. a layer-choice change rather than a new mechanism.
